paragraphs.title: The Person Who Fears the Lord and the Blessing of His Household

answers: The man that feareth the LORD
The man who is angry with the wicked
The man who gives no charity
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Blessed is the man that feareth the LORD.”

easy.q: What does the man who fears the LORD greatly delight in?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Wealth and riches shall be in his house.”
easy.q: What is mentioned as a blessing in his house?

answers: The fear of the LORD is connected with blessed seed, a prosperous house, and enduring righteousness
The fear of the LORD causes a person to avoid everyone
The fear of the LORD brings anger
medium.explanation: The passage connects fearing the LORD with blessed descendants, household prosperity, and righteousness that endures.
medium.q: How are the fear of the LORD and blessing connected in this passage?

medium.explanation: “Delighteth greatly” means takes great pleasure in or strongly desires.
Verse 3 says, “his righteousness endureth for ever.”
medium.q: What is said to endure for ever?

answers: Fearing the LORD and delighting in His commandments, followed by blessing in the household and enduring righteousness
Darkness, evil tidings, and finally defeat
challenge.explanation: The verses begin with devotion to the LORD and continue with blessed descendants, household prosperity, and enduring righteousness.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 1–3?

answers: They will belong among the upright and receive blessing
challenge.explanation: The verse describes his seed as mighty and connected with the blessed generation of the upright.
challenge.q: What does “the generation of the upright shall be blessed” indicate about the man’s seed?

answers: Both are presented as blessings associated with the man
Both cause the wicked to triumph
Both are connected with fear of darkness
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 mentions both “wealth and riches” and righteousness that endures for ever.
challenge.q: What connects wealth in the house with righteousness?

paragraphs.title: The Light, Goodness, and Stability of the Righteous

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness.”
easy.q: What arises in the darkness for the upright?

easy.explanation: The verse describes him as “gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.”
easy.q: Which qualities are named in the righteous person?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “A good man sheweth favour, and lendeth.”
easy.q: What does the good man do?

answers: Light arises for him, and he remains gracious and righteous
medium.explanation: Light arises to the upright in darkness, and the person is described as gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
medium.q: How does the righteous person respond to darkness?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that he conducts or manages his affairs with wisdom and good judgment.
medium.q: What does “guide his affairs with discretion” mean?

answers: He is not moved, and his memory remains
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says, “he shall not be moved for ever,” and that the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.
medium.q: What is the result of the righteous man’s way of life?

answers: Giving and lending are joined with wise conduct and not being moved
Giving only makes the wicked angry
Giving is presented as a cause of fear
challenge.explanation: The good man gives and lends wisely, and the passage then describes the righteous as firmly established.
challenge.q: What connection is made between generosity and stability?

answers: The righteous person brings good in the present and leaves a lasting legacy
The righteous person hides his deeds
The righteous person loses his position
challenge.explanation: Light represents present help and goodness, while everlasting remembrance indicates lasting influence and stability.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the movement from light in darkness to everlasting remembrance?

answers: Because he gives and lends wisely
Because he is angry with the poor
challenge.explanation: Wise discretion fits the good man who shows favour and lends responsibly.
challenge.q: Why is guiding his affairs with discretion fitting for this person?

paragraphs.title: A Trusting Heart and Charity to the Poor

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “He shall not be afraid of evil tidings.”
easy.q: What is the righteous person not afraid of?

easy.explanation: The verse says that his heart is fixed, “trusting in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the righteous person’s heart trust?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “He hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor.”
easy.q: To whom does the righteous person give?

answers: Because his heart is fixed and trusts in the LORD
Because he is angry with everyone
medium.explanation: The passage connects freedom from fear with a heart that is fixed and trusting in the LORD.
medium.q: Why is the righteous person not afraid of evil tidings?

answers: His heart is settled and steadfast
His heart is full of anger
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a stable and confident heart that is not easily frightened.
medium.q: What does “his heart is established” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: Verse 9 repeats that “his righteousness endureth for ever.”
medium.q: What is said about the righteousness of the giver?

answers: Trust enables the righteous person to face danger and give to the poor
Trust causes him to stop helping others
challenge.explanation: His trusting heart keeps him from fear, and he is also described as giving generously to the poor.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage show between trust and generosity?

answers: The righteous person and his work remain stable and honoured
The righteous person falls and is forgotten
challenge.explanation: His righteousness endures, and his horn is exalted with honour, showing continuing stability and dignity.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the repeated ideas of enduring and being exalted?

answers: The righteous person trusts and gives, while the wicked person is angry and loses his desire
The righteous person is angry, while the wicked person gives
challenge.explanation: The righteous person is steadfast and generous, while the wicked person is grieved, angry, and ultimately loses his desire.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the righteous person’s response to evil tidings and the wicked person’s response at the end of the psalm?

paragraphs.title: The Anger and Defeat of the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “The wicked shall see it, and be grieved.”
easy.q: What does the wicked person do when he sees the righteous?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “he shall gnash with his teeth.”
easy.q: What does the wicked person do with his teeth?

easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “the desire of the wicked shall perish.”
easy.q: What happens to the desire of the wicked?

medium.explanation: The verse begins by saying that the wicked sees the righteous and is grieved.
medium.q: What causes the wicked person’s anger?

medium.explanation: In the context of grief and gnashing teeth, “melt away” indicates weakness and collapse.
medium.q: What does “melt away” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: The final statement says that the desire of the wicked shall perish.
medium.q: What is the result of the wicked person’s anger?

answers: The wicked person is angry and weakened, while the righteous person prospers and remains stable
The wicked person gives, while the righteous person gnashes his teeth
The wicked person trusts, while the righteous person fears
challenge.explanation: The wicked person responds with grief and anger, while the righteous person has previously been shown to be secure and enduring.
challenge.q: What contrast is created between the wicked person and the righteous person?

answers: They will perish and not be accomplished
They will become acts of charity
challenge.explanation: “The desire of the wicked shall perish” shows that his aims will fail.
challenge.q: What does the ending teach about the wicked person’s goals?

answers: From seeing and grief to gnashing teeth, weakness, and the loss of desire
From giving to joy and honour
From fear to trust and charity
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a progression from seeing the righteous, to grief, gnashing teeth, melting away, and finally the perishing of desire.
challenge.q: How does the wicked person’s condition develop within the verse?
